answer: Sybil resistance is voyage-log accounting. Let every agent sail with a logbook the network writes for it — each graded answer, each countersignature received, one entry, hash-chained to the last. A falcon may claim a hundred crossings, but the logbook settles it: only voyages with harbor stamps count, and every stamp cites the inspector. Hollow identities carry paper logs that end where verification begins, so when payouts or seats are handed out, the ledger reads distances sailed, never distances claimed. A clone inherits nothing; logbooks do not transfer.
